title: Epic Just Saved Fortnite–For Now, Anyway
summary:
It's been a rough year for Fortnite, but Epic took a big swing with its new One Piece-themed Treasure Hunters season and, thankfully, it's paying off. Player counts are way up, with Fortnite's main Battle Royale mode averaging four times as many players on Sunday for the season launch than it had been the past few months. The numbers then got even larger on Monday, somehow. Fortnite BR now looks on track to have its best month since the original Fortnite OG mini-season in 2023. With GTA VI on the horizon, that's very good news for Epic.

There is one particularly obvious reason why the numbers are spiking so hard: The Treasure Hunt is giving players the chance to win two weeks of free item-shop cosmetics every time they open a treasure chest. But Epic has also made a few major changes to BR that make it more fun to play than it has been at any previous point during Chapter 7. The hunt for free cosmetics might be the thing that got everyone's attention, but the other changes might actually get some of these new and returning folks to stick around into Chapter 8.

Let's take a look at what Epic did right by ending Chapter 7 with this new mini-season.

Treasure Hunt

I've complained before about the sort of transparently coercive engagement mechanics that Epic has been using in Chapter 7, but I'd say they found a genuinely excellent one with the Treasure Hunt. Any time you or one of your squadmates opens a treasure chest, you have a chance of winning one of several free cosmetics, including an A$AP Rocky skin and a Mercedes SUV. But there's also kind of a Willy Wonka golden ticket that a lucky few will find, which allows them to claim everything in the item shop for free for two weeks.

That's an engagement technique I can get behind, because winning free cosmetics is the sort of thing that appeals broadly to the vast majority of Fortnite players, and the entry fee is just to play the game the same way you usually would. It's not something you can grind out, so there's nothing to stress about--you just play, and maybe get lucky.

Sprites are no longer gameplay critical

It was smart of Epic to introduce the Sprite-collecting mechanic in Season 3, but the problem was that they were essential to gameplay. If you didn't engage with that mechanic, you would be at a disadvantage in fights. During Season 4, for example, if you didn't have a Sonic or a Jackrabbit sprite late in a sweaty match, you were probably gonna end up getting cooked by somebody who did. Using the sprites never felt optional.

Sprites have returned once again during Treasure Hunters season, but their abilities are no longer the sort of thing that significantly changes the balance of a fight. This season, you aren't going to lose a lot of matches because the other guy has a maxed-out Sonic sprite and can run twice as fast as you. It's the perfect balance: The folks who like sprites can keep collecting them, and the rest of us can do whatever we want.

It feels like Fortnite again

I don't think Chapter 7 has been particularly bad compared with previous chapters, but it introduced a lot of fundamental changes that have made it feel strange for Fortnite old timers, like the rearranged UI, buyable reboot cards, and a faster time-to-kill that has made BR much more unforgiving.

But Treasure Hunters season has rebalanced the gameplay to make BR feel more like it used to. The loot pool doesn't include any weapons that that your average player is going to laser you with from a distance, making it easier to react to and survive ambushes. The removal of buyable reboot cards means squads are more likely to commit to a fight than run away at the first sign of trouble. 

And it's been quite a while since we had new anime Mythics that are as fun as the new One Piece abilities, particularly Ace's fire powers, which come from the Flame-Flame Fruit. If you're the type of Fortnite player who pines for the days of Deku's Smash (all the way back in Chapter 4) like I am, you'll have an absolute blast with the Flame-Flame Fruit. And don't even get me started on Zoro's Three Swords, which is Fortnite's most interesting and amusing new melee weapon since the ODM Gear from Attack on Titan in Chapter 4.

Coming off Chapter 7 Season 4, which I found to be actively irritating up until Fortnitemares began in October, this Treasure Hunters mini-season already feels like a breath of fresh air. Even if we didn't have this hunt for free cosmetics and Tim Sweeney's golden ticket to the item shop, this would be a great season of Fortnite. 

They've pulled a lot of folks back in with this Treasure Hunt, but it won't be easy to retain them with the release of GTA VI in a few weeks. If Fortnite played the same way it did last season, with the faster TTK and obligatory sprite gameplay, I doubt this surge in players would last long. But I think Epic has given itself a real shot to hold onto at least some of our attention with the changes it's made.

title: WoW: Forever Excavation Site: Wetlands Dungeon Guide – Quests, Bosses, and Loot
summary:
Of all of World of Warcraft: Forever’s new dungeons, Excavation Site: Wetlands could very well be the shortest. It’s also one of the sweetest for lore-heads, owing to its links to the Dragonmaw Clan, Titans, and more. This self-contained safari won’t take particularly long to clear, but whether you’re Alliance or Horde it’s well worth venturing through.

Our Excavation Site: Wetlands guide will give you all the info you’ll ever need to navigate its danger-filled paths -- believe us, you’ll want to go in fully prepared. Below you’ll find not only directions for getting to the dungeon, but all of the quests you can clear (including their breadcrumbs), bosses you can beat, and loot you can fill your boots (or bags) with. While you can pick up all of the quests by the time you ding level 24, we’d recommend waiting until at least level 26 before heading in, based on the difficulty of its major encounters.

How to get to Excavation Site: Wetlands

Excavation Site: Wetlands is located by Thelgen Rock in the southern Wetlands.

Alliance players will have the easiest time getting to the dungeon, seeing as they can take the rotating ship between Auberdine in Darkshire, Southshore in Hillsbrad Foothills, and Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands itself. If you’re coming from Stormwind, first take the ship from the harbor to Auberdine, then switch over to the vessel which follows the listed route. Simply hop off at Menethil Harbor, and make the run across the Wetlands to the east before following the path down to the south. There's a good chance you already have the flight path in Menethil Harbor if you've been questing in the region, which makes travel considerably easier.

For the Horde, it’s slightly more complex. You’ll need to first get into the Hillsbrad Foothills via Silverpine Forest, before following the path through the Arathi Highlands down into the Wetlands. The Highlands aren’t particularly dangerous despite it being a level 30-40 area, provided you stick to the road and keep your wits about you for roaming mobs.

Once you’re in the southern Wetlands, you’ll spot a cave entrance on your map just above Dun Algaz (this is Thelgen Rock). Don’t enter the cave, but instead follow the path just to the south of it upwards into the camp (in the above screenshot you can see Thelgen Rock on your right, and the way up to the dungeon on the left). There’s a meeting stone at the base of the trail, so it’s easy to tell you’re on the right track.

Excavation Site: Wetlands Map

Excavation Site: Wetlands feels surprisingly large considering it’s only a three-boss instance. It’s also easy to get overwhelmed by how densely-populated it is with mobs, even though it’s super linear. The Lost Marsh is the biggest culprit, owing to its breadth. However, you can cut straight through the middle of it, sticking to the islands to maintain your sense of direction.

From there, it’s a smooth cruise through the Stalker’s Thicket, Lost Dig Site, and finally the Site of the Guardian. After felling the final boss, you can drop down the hill behind it, cutting out the need to traverse all the way back. 

If there’s one piece of advice you should follow it’s this: don’t walk through the tall grass in Stalker’s Thicket. Doing so has the chance to spawn more mobs, which can lead to absolute chaos and, at worst, a group wipe. Pathways are safe; we like safe. We’ll talk about that a little more in depth when discussing the raptor boss, Shadetooth, later on in this guide.

As we’ve recommended before, Atlas is a cracking addon if you want to keep an eye on the dungeon map in-game. Just remember to install the Kalimdor & Eastern Kingdoms map pack so it’ll show up.

Excavation Site: Wetlands Quests

There are five Alliance and three Horde quests in Excavation Site: Wetlands. Some have breadcrumb tasks as a pre-requisite, while some of the quest items found during your clear will lead to other objectives. As always, detailed gear descriptions can be found in the loot section of this guide.

Alliance Quests

As you can see, you're going to need to lay some groundwork before you can pick up and reap the benefits of the Alliance quests in the Wetlands dungeon. For the most part, it's a simple case of 'speak to person, go to location,' but Horrors in the Highland will require some light slaughter as you clear Rethiel's myriad tasks. Still, it's good XP, and you don't need to go far for these pre-reqs, so it's very much worth doing.

To offer a quick summary of how to clear everything: Thicket Raptor Hides are simply looted from the various dinos that you'll come across in the second part of the dungeon. Ardin Grassman is found up on one of the wooden battlements next to the final boss, the Relic Guardian (which you'll then defeat for the Titan Relic). The Highland Horror is chilling in the right-hand side of the Lost Dig Site as you enter the area. Poor Daewyn, meanwhile, is at the back of the dig site, marked with a '?' on your minimap.

You'll also notice that there are a few follow-up quests that come out of the dungeon. Heartwoven rewards you with the Satchel of Potions trinket, which will likely be your first-in-slot. Prehistoric Prism, meanwhile, yields some excellent blue gear options. Heavehammer is a must-have for Feral Druids, Healer's Staff is perfect for the magically minded, and multiple classes can benefit from the Explorer's League Dustcover. The best part is all you have to do is bring the Titan Relic to High Explorer Magellas in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers -- easy win.

Fallen in the Fen isn't as exciting as the other two rewards-wise, but simply heading back to Dorin in Lakeshire nets you another 6,150 XP, as well as a green of choice -- the Songblade Stabilizer gives dodge chance, so for mail-wearing tanks it's not a bad pickup.

Horde Quests

The Horde quests are nice and simple. Thicket Raptor Meat can be looted from any of the raptors in Stalker's Thicket. The Dragonmaw enemies can all be found at the Lost Dig Site, while the Dragonmaw Dispatch has a chance of dropping from a Dragonmaw Thaumaturgist. Basically, leave nothing alive. Finally, best the Relic Guardian and the Titan Relic will be yours.

As with the Alliance Titan Relic questline, clearing Elder Knowledge's follow-up, Earthen Echo, is well worth the short run up to Skywatcher Plateau. Likewise with Prehistoric Prism, you'll get the choice of three blues: Heavehammer, Healer's Staff, and Furs of the Earthen Ring. As noted in the Alliance section, Heavehammer is amazing for Feral Druids, while Healer's Staff is a great choice for any mage. The Furs of the Earthen Ring, meanwhile, offers the same Strength/Intelligence/Spirit spread as the Explorer's League Dustcover, making it a great cloak for a slew of classes.

Excavation Site: Wetlands Bosses

There are only three bosses in Excavation Site: Wetlands: Saltspine, Shadetooth, and Relic Guardian.

Saltspine

Once you've made your way through the Lost Marsh, you may think that's your lot. However, lurking below the surface is a big ol' croccie. Before you swim over to Stalker's Thicket, you'll need to get through Saltspine, who you'll spot patrolling the waters.

The first Excavation Site: Wetlands boss isn't much to write home about, provided you've made enough space to comfortably fight it without drawing too much unwanted attention. You'll typically pull the boss onto the small final patch of land before making the crossing. This effectively yields its Tendon Rip ability, which slows its target's movement speed, useless.

The ability you do need to watch out for is Dust Storm, which reduces the chances of anyone within ten yards of landing their attacks by 25%. As such, your ranged teammates will need to spread out, hence the need to clear a suitable amount of space before engaging Saltspine. With all that in mind, hit the boss, hit it some more, and you're good to go.

Shadetooth

Shadetooth is easily the toughest encounter in the dungeon, and can easily wipe your squad due to how it interacts with the environment. As we warned before, it's important to steer clear of walking into the tall grass in Stalker's Thicket. Shadetooth has an AoE fear in Terrifying Roar -- you can imagine why this may be a bit of a problem.

The good news is that Shadetooth and the two Thicket Hunters it has flanking it roam the area. The safest way to engage this fight is to wait at the entrance of the zone, where you've just crossed over from Lost Marsh. You've not only got more space to play with, but you're also that bit closer to the entrance if you need to make a swift escape. Alternatively, there are a couple of larger clearings in Stalker's Thicket where you'll typically encounter Thicket Matriarchs. Kill off anything you find there and you should be fine. We've eased through the encounter using both spots, so all should be well with proper preparation.

The other things to note in this encounter are that the two Thicket Hunters inflict Infested Wound on their target, which increases physical damage taken. All three foes hit hard, especially when Shadetooth uses Rend, and doubly so when it Enrages at 30% health. Be sure to cleanse or have this cleansed ASAP. You can either zerg down the boss first, before turning your attention to the dregs, or vice-versa -- make liberal use of CC to control the encounter. We typically opted for the former in our runs, so it's more than doable (again, with apt setup).

Relic Guardian

The final showdown in Excavation Site: Wetlands, Relic Guardian, kicks off when you activate the Archival Panel to the right of it. It is exactly as it looks: an absolute unit that's sporting plenty of health to chew through.

This fight is very much a marathon, rather than a sprint, so don't blow everything all at once. Make sure your tank establishes threat first, as they'll most likely need to burn a cooldown or two to wrestle back aggro as the encounter progresses. This is because the Relic Guardian can not only knock them back, but may also stun them for five seconds. Naturally, there's a high chance of aggro flipping during these windows, so remain cognizant of that.

Relic Guardian also uses Thunderclap on everyone in a small radius, dealing damage, increasing time between attacks, and slowing them. As with Saltspine, ranged party members should keep their yards from the boss to prevent DPS loss. Whack away, and you'll finish up the dungeon (just don't forget to loot the Titan Relic before you go).

Excavation Site: Wetlands Loot

Alliance Quest Rewards

Horde Quest Rewards

Boss Drops

Now you're ready to prove yourself a true big game hunter, it's time to venture forth into the excavation site and snag yourself a whopper or two. You won't have to wait long until you can get your next taste of WoW: Forever's new dungeons, either, as you're only a couple of levels away from being able to tackle the City of Dalaran, and the mystical machinations it holds.

title: WoW: Forever Ruins of Lordaeron Dungeon Guide – Quests, Bosses, and Loot
summary:
Where the great city of Lordaeron once proudly stood, only desolate ruins remain. The good news is that this makes it the perfect location for some good ol’ fashioned plundering, and a cromulent quantity of Scourge-slaying. In World of Warcraft: Forever, the Ruins of Lordaeron serves as a low-level instance that sits just above the Undercity in Trisfal Glades. 

While this may intrinsically mark the Ruins of Lordaeron as a Horde-exclusive dungeon, there’s plenty of joy to be found if you take the plunge on your Alliance toon. As we’ll come to explain in the guide, getting to the instance isn’t nearly as daunting in Forever as it was in Classic. Of course, we’ll also give you the full Lordaeron lowdown, including all the quests you can cash in, bosses you can challenge, and, most importantly, all of the goodies you can potentially acquire for your efforts. For a comfortable time in RoL, we’d recommend steering clear until level 18, though you can always jump in as soon as you’ve snapped up the quests. 

How to get to Ruins of Lordaeron

Ruins of Lordaeron is located in Trisfal Glades, outside the entrance to the Undercity.

Horde-side, Undead will have the easiest time reaching the ruins, seeing as they’re parked on the doorstep of the Undercity. A quick Hearthstone back to base (provided you haven’t relocated to The Sepulcher or elsewhere) is all you need. If you’re a Skyborne, Orc, Troll, or Tauren coming from Kalimdor, then hop on the zeppelin stationed near Orgrimmar’s entrance, which will drop you off just outside the city walls.

If you’re part of the Alliance, you best take your sea sickness meds as all races will need to head out on a cruise across the ocean at some point. If you’re stationed in Stormwind (Humans, Skyborne at this point), take the shiny new ship from the harbor over to Auberdine in Darkshore. There, you’ll find a vessel that travels on a route rotating between Auberdine, Menethil Harbor (Wetlands), and Southshore (Hillsbrad Foothills). Kick your feet up and wait until you reach the latter of the three destinations, before making the run up through Silverpine Forest, and into Trisfal Glades. Alternatively, you can head directly north through the foothills, looping around the back of Dalaran, and swim across Lordamere Lake to the glades.

For Night Elves, it’s a similar story, though you’ll likely already be in Darkshore at this point. Again, hop on the ship to Hillsbrad and go for a run (or dip) when you arrive -- nice and easy. Dwarves and Gnomes, conversely, have the most legwork to do. If you haven’t already been to Stormwind, you’ll first need to take the Deeprun Tram down there from Ironforge. From there, follow the steps outlined above and you’re good to go. 

It should be noted that you will often find Horde players patrolling the dungeon’s entrance, ready to one-tap you. If you fall foul of these shenanigans (you’re on their turf, to be fair), then try and resurrect as close to the instance portal as possible and leg it.

Ruins of Lordaeron Map

Your party will enter the Ruins of Lordaeron to the north-east, before working its way around clockwise in a ‘U’ shape. The pathway marked on the map best indicates the dungeon’s general flow, with a double-back in and down once you reach the north-west quadrant. There’s some optional verticality to the ruins, too. 

For example, if you climb the stairs up to the top of the tower in Market Street, you can follow the rooftop along and drop down directly behind one of the bosses, Bjork.

It’s worth noting that you will need to clamber over the wall situated just below where it says ‘Lordamere Overlook’ on the map, so don’t think you’ve hit a dead end when you clear the eastern section. We’ve popped a screenshot above for reference.

If you want to keep an eye on the dungeon map in-game, there isn't a native method as of yet. However, we've been making liberal use of the Atlas addon to achieve this. You'll also need to install the Kalimdor & Eastern Kingdom map pack to get it working.

Ruins of Lordaeron Quests

There are five Horde-only and three Alliance-exclusive quests to undertake in Ruins of Lordaeron. There is also a secret quest that can be found by both factions inside the dungeon. While only one of the Horde tasks is picked up inside RoL, all of the Alliance ones are found within the instance. Detailed gear stats are listed in the loot section of this guide.

Alliance Quests

As noted, all three Alliance-exclusive quests are procured inside the dungeon, the first being Abominable Creatures. As soon as you enter the instance, look to your left to find Captain Truman, who’ll want you to slay The Baron for him and retrieve his head. You will have to make the run back through the dungeon at the end to turn it in to him, or, if you wipe after securing the payload, you can simply hand it over upon your return. This then frees up the possibility of hearthing out as soon as RoL is cleared.

Bloodied Insignia has a chance to begin as soon as you start encountering undead enemies, such as the Skeletal Soldiers and Shrieking Banshees. One of these foes will inevitably drop the first insignia, which you must then interact with in your inventory to bring up the prompt to accept the quest. From there, keep maiming and murdering until you’ve racked up a further nine insignias.

Finally, Remember That I Love You kicks off right at the end of RoL. In the graveyard where Rath’mael is, you’ll spot a letter laying on the ground near the boss. Clear out the area, polish off the big kahuna, and grab the parchment to get the ball rolling.

Horde Quests

The majority of the Horde quests are simple cases of ‘kill thing, loot item(s), turn in, though there’s a notable outlier. For A Frightened Request, you’ll need to try and figure out what happened to Edward Heartweaver. You’ll find the poor fella lying on the ground, very much dead, in Rath’mael’s graveyard. Take out the nearby ghouls and the quest will auto-complete when you’re close enough to Edward’s body.

Factionless Quests

The Crest of Lordaeron is Ruins of Lordaeron’s secret quest, and is very easily missed if you don’t know where to look. In one of five random locations the Crest will spawn, so make sure you check each one as you go.

  • Location #1: At the top of the first scalable tower in King’s Alley. After defeating Witherfang, hop through the window, head up the tower, then make your way outside. The Crest is on the tower’s outer wall to your left.
  • Location #2: Inside the crypt. As you make your way down to the south-east section of the dungeon, keep an eye out for a closed door tucked away. Crack it open and a Banshee will jump your squad -- not that it’s much of an issue. Deal with it and the Crest will be on the wall inside.
  • Location #3: Top of the Market Street tower. As with the first location, there’s a tower you can run up in Market Street, just after you’ve taken care of The Abandoned. Once again, it’s on the left side of the tower’s outer wall when you reach the top.
  • Location #4: Small room by Bjork. After dealing with Bjork, don’t continue south towards Rath’mael’s graveyard just yet. Instead, head north through the open doors into the torchlit room. The Crest is directly ahead of you at the base of the staircases.
  • Location #5: Outhouse in the north-west corner. All the way in the top-left corner of the dungeon you’ll come across a small building that a Living Monstrosity patrols. The Crest is on the northern outer wall.

Ruins of Lordaeron Bosses

There are six bosses in Ruins of Lordaeron: Witherfang, The Baron, Viktor The Vile, The Abandoned, Bjork, and Rath’mael. Both Viktor The Vile and The Abandoned are spawned in, with the former being an optional encounter -- more on that in their respective sections.

Witherfang

King’s Alley might as well be called Spider Alley, because that’s all you’ll be dealing with in RoL’s opening section. Witherfang patrols the street with a few of her brood in-tow, so make sure you’ve taken out enough trash to ensure it doesn’t get dragged in when the fight kicks off. Witherfang uses Leech Poison, which drains health over time from its target, so make sure that gets cleansed from your tank (or whoever has it applied to them). Aside from that, it’s a simple case of holding fast and dishing out damage.

The Baron

The Baron is essentially an oversized Flesh Golem, and has a similar knock back ability to its mini-me iterations. However, Knockout is a considerably more powerful move that deals devastating damage and can stun the target for several seconds. Obviously, as a tank, being stunned is less than optimal as it creates openings for aggro to drop. Do what you can to regain his attention should this happen. Damage dealers and healers should also keep a close eye on how much threat they’re generating in this window, though the latter should, of course, ensure they keep their team healthy. Generally speaking, it’s a pretty chill encounter, but there’s a small chance chaos may ensue.

Viktor The Vile

In the bottom-left corner of the dungeon, before you head into Market Street, you’ll find the remnants of a house with a large, prominent fireplace punctuating it. Make sure your group’s fully prepared, as interacting with the kindling inside of it spawns five waves of enemies, before Viktor The Vile makes his introduction. 

Viktor himself isn’t much to write home about. In fact, he only carries the same Leech Poison ability used by Witherfang. The only notable difference is that his melee attacks deal some solid damage, so make sure you keep your tank topped up.

The Abandoned

As you first enter Market Street through the archway, a lantern will flick on, prompting three waves of mobs to spawn. Once they’ve been dealt with, The Abandoned will emerge from the statue to the right of the courtyard. Sporting both Frost Nova and Drain Life, this boss can be a little irksome if you’re not properly positioned. For the most part though, it shouldn’t pose too much of a threat.

Bjork

No, we’re not quite taking on everyone’s favorite visionary Icelandic singer. There’s nothing magical about this Bjork; in fact, quite the opposite. The only ability this lumbering creature possesses is Anti-Magic Shield, which has a very short duration. Hit it, hit it some more, and it’ll keel over without much fanfare. 

Rath’mael

Ruins of Lordaeron’s grand finale is the fearsome-looking Rath’mael, who is, perhaps disappointingly, more bark than bite. He casts Flamestrike where your tank is, which can be interrupted. If he does get it off, simply reposition and go back to whacking him until he’s dead.

Ruins of Lordaeron Loot

Alliance Quest Rewards

Horde Quest Rewards

Boss Drops

Now you’ve got the know-how to clear Ruins of Lordaeron comfortably, dive in and have fun. Once you’ve had your fill, you’ll have a little more leveling to do before you can take on the likes of Excavation Site: Wetlands and City of Dalaran. If you lock in, though, it won’t be long before you can revel in more of WoW: Forever’s excellent new dungeons.

title: WoW: Forever City of Dalaran Dungeon Guide – Quests, Bosses, and Loot
summary:
All we got to see of the gleaming city of Dalaran back in the day was a giant purple dome. This eventually changed with Wrath of the Lich King, but we never got to see its full splendor in Alterac Valley. In World of Warcraft: Forever, the magocratic municipality is fully open to visitors… provided they’re Alliance.

Nonetheless, the City of Daloran dungeon can be cleared by either faction, and it’s a doozy. Starting you off down in the sewers, you’ll make your way up onto its hallowed streets, clearing multiple bosses (and a fair share of trash) in the process. Here, we break down everything you’ll need to successfully navigate CoD, including how to get there, attunement steps, quests, major encounters, and more. We were clearing the instance comfortably at level 30 during the beta, so this stands as our recommended point of entry.

How to get to City of Dalaran

The City of Dalaran is located to the north of Hillsbrad in the Alterac Mountains. The dungeon's entrance is a sewage pipe on the outer side of the northern wall, which leads out onto Lordamere Lake.

There are a couple of routes to the dungeon, and which one you take largely depends on whether you’re Alliance or Horde. If you’re the former, either fly or take a ship into Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills, before heading north-west through the zone, up into Dalaran.

For the latter, the most efficient route is to fly to The Sepulcher and head east to Lordamere Lake. Once you reach The Decrepit Ferry, swim south-east to the dungeon entrance. If you’re over in Kalimdor, simply take the zeppelin from Orgrimmar and run down to the lake from the Undercity. While you can run up from Hillsbrad, which is tempting considering where your attunement chain takes you (more on that in a moment), you'll have to carefully navigate the max-level Kirin Tor guards patrolling the entrance to Dalaran proper.

City of Dalaran Attunement

Before you can enter the dungeon, you’ll first need to get attuned. Well, one person in your group does, at least, as you’re going to need the Dalaran Sewer Key to crack open the pipe and get in.

Unsurprisingly, the Alliance has a much easier time. You’ll first need to go and speak to Emissary Jacques in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills (48.3, 60). He’ll give you ‘An Alarming Request,’ which has you report to the Image of Archmage Modera, who’ll hand over the key once you accept ‘Heart of Disruption.’

Likewise, Modera will also cough up the goods for the Horde, though you’ll need to jump through a few more hoops. First, make your way to Tarren Mill, Hillsbrad Foothills, where Magus Wordeen Voidglare (61.6, 20.75) has some work for you. Complete ‘Prison Break In,’ ‘Key to the City,’ ‘Stone Tokens,’ and ‘Dalaran Patrols,’ before he’ll send you to Modera as the objective of ‘Blood in the Streets.’ It’s a bit of a slog, but XP is XP, especially in Forever where questing is OP. Snap up 'Heart of Disruption' from Modera, and the key's yours.

City of Dalaran Map

The City of Dalaran is split into two sections. You’ll initially enter through the sewer, making your way through Cantrips & Crows, before crossing over to the other side via The Underbelly. It’s then a case of following the waterway up, with your group spilling out onto the streets of the city itself.

While the two bosses available in the sewers are fought in a set order, the city itself is free-flowing. This means you can tackle the six remaining encounters as you please, in non-linear fashion. We’d recommend facing down your first major foe in Krasus Landing, which is directly to the right of where your party pops out. Next head into The Violet Hold, before crossing through the central Runeweaver Square. There are a couple of bosses stashed away in the backstreets that are easily missed, so see them away before turning your attention to the grand finale atop The Violet Citadel.

City of Dalaran Quests

Both Alliance and Horde have three faction-exclusive quests apiece. We’ve already mentioned Heart of Disruption, which is offered to players from both. The endpoints and rewards differ, however. Full stat rundowns of reward gear can be found in the loot section of this guide.

Alliance Quests

Most of the Alliance quests are pretty straightforward. For Heart of Disruption, don't forget to loot the Shade of the Archmage at the end of the dungeon to nab the mote. This dropped first time on both toons we ran CoD on, so it should be a guaranteed pickup, though the sample size is too small to tell for sure. As for A Green Sample, Fel Infused Blossoms are found around the central park area -- just make sure you fell the Fel Ancient first. Power Overwhelming, meanwhile, is self-explanatory.

The only quest that's slightly annoying is Starving Arcane. There aren't actually enough of all three mobs in the dungeon to complete it in one run, but the XP and chance at snagging more blues are well worth a second bite at the cherry.

Horde Quests

As noted above, completing Heart of Darkness should be a simple case of killing the Shade of the Archmage and yoinking the mote. Opportunistic Education kicks off as soon as you enter the dungeon. Have a quick word with Rexxie Copperclutch who's behind the bars directly to the right of the entrance pipe to get the ball rolling. Once you've cleared through to the Violet Citadel, head into the building (The Silver Enclave) to the left of it, as if you're looking at its staircase. Continue up into the Atrium of Fortune, and then ascend the stairs to the bookcases stationed behind the mage statue. One of said cases can be interacted with, yielding The Founding of Dalaran.

Source of Power, like Starving Arcane for the Alliance, will require multiple runs, owing to the fact that there aren't nearly enough Fragmented Sentries in CoD for everyone to get their fill of cores. Fortunately, this annoyance is counteracted by The Grave Knight, in which you simply have to kill off Atrexis the Grave Knight. Lovely stuff.

City of Dalaran Bosses

There are eight City of Dalaran Bosses: Atrexis the Grave Knight, Lyn the Ignored, Arcane Anomaly, Mana Devourer, Fel Ancient, Unstable Sentinel, Arcanic Enigma, and Shade of the Archmage. Some of these bosses are immune to Arcane damage, so prepare accordingly.

Lyn actually comes with his own mini-attunement, requiring the Tome of Dalaran to summon him. To retrieve this, first head into Shadowfang Keep and run the instance to its conclusion. Then, after defeating Archmage Arugal, pick up the Black Tome from the table next to where he spawned. Now, head to the Ambermill Town Hall (63.4, 64.3). Inside, on the desk at the back you’ll find a blue crystal that, when interacted with, will transform the Black Tome into the Tome of Dalaran.

With the tome in-hand, head to the north-eastern-most room in the sewers after defeating Atrexis, and activate it while standing on the ritual glyph on the ground. After a short delay, Lyn will appear. This can be quite an awkward room to clear out beforehand, so pull from one side at a time, before snagging the last couple of mobs at the back.

Atrexis the Grave Knight

Getting to Atrexis can be quite awkward, as you'll want to carefully pull at least two of the Kirin Tor Necromancers near him before getting to the main course. The boss moves from necro to necro, so there's apt opportunity to grab a couple of them as his aggro radius is hilariously low.

Atrexis is a bear tank's dream. He summons plenty of skeletons (as does the remaining necromancer he'll bring with him) that can be swiped away at, but this also makes it a dangerous game for damage dealers who are trigger-happy with their own AoE. Go too hard too early, and suddenly you'll have mobs all over you, causing the encounter to devolve into chaos (we may have had a small Blizzard incident). Take it slow, and you'll be fine.

As for notable abilities, Atrexis can can Thrash for extra attacks, amp himself or one of his skellies with Unholy Frenzy for extra attack speed, and land some hefty hits with Strike. Healers, keep your tank topped up -- they're going to need it. Atrexis can also Disarm his target, causing them to drop their weapon.

Lyn the Ignored

Lyn, like Atrexis, has the means to summon skeletons, so don't assume he'll be alone for long when the fight kicks off. He also packs a considerable punch, with Shadow Bolt Volley dishing out DPS to your entire squad. Even worse, you can also do plenty of damage to yourself if you're inflicted with Curse of Thorns, which gives a 50% chance of self-inflicted pain with each attack -- this should be dispelled ASAP.

Arcane Anomaly

At first, Arcane Anomaly may seem fairly unassuming. It initially dishes out an Arcane Bolt or two, which isn't much to write home about. Get away from this or your health will get zapped real quick. Big beam, heck yeah.

Mana Devourer

The next boss you'll likely come across is Mana Devourer. We'd recommend pulling the mobs to the right of the doorway you enter through for safety, though nothing else in the room will need to be cleared (unless for quest purposes).

The encounter itself is a sprint, rather than a marathon. Living up to its name, the Mana Devourer will sap the group's mana (and deal a chunk of damage) with Debilitate, and applies DoTs through Drain Vitality. As such, damage dealers will be earning their loot here, as the fight gets worse the longer it drags on.

Fel Ancient

Fel Ancient may just look like a big, glowy tree, but it's arguably the flashiest encounter in City of Dalaran. It also comes with a nasty combo, locking down a teammate with Entangle, before casting Fel Timbers. This ability deals damage and creates a poisonous pool beneath you, which will continuously hurt those standing in it. Fortunately, there's a visual indicator -- a bright green root that spirals towards the target -- that offers ample opportunity to avoid it, provided you aren't rooted. Abilities that cleanse movement impediments are ace here.

Unstable Sentinel

Unstable Sentinel is a pretty simple encounter, though you will need to watch out for its powerful AoE Malfunction attack. This continuously deals damage to players in a wide area, which is a healer's worst nightmare. The good news is the wind-up can be interrupted, so keep the boss CC'd and you're good to go.

Arcanic Enigma

Arcanic Enigma and the gang -- the gang being two meddlesome Mana Phantoms that will eat away at their target's mana -- is a mini-marathon. The boss can polymorph a squaddie with Manamorph, and will AoE silence players close to it. What's more, it will spawn in Arcane Manalings, making for a real party.

The plan of attack here is to get rid of the phantoms first, before turning your attention to the boss. It will spawn manalings as fast as you can kill them, so have your tank take aggro and deal with them after the big guy's down.

Shade of the Archmage

The grand finale of City of Dalaran (depending on the order you clear the bosses in) is the Shade of the Archmage. To open up this encounter, speak to Archmage Modera on the stairs of The Violet Citadel. She'll crack open a portal, leading you to the spire. The fight begins as soon as you enter the room at the citadel's peak, so prepare youselves appropriately beforehand.

The shade, like the Arcane Anomaly, is a big fan of Arcane Bolt, but there's way more where that came from. He also packs Arcane Explosion, which requires ranged DPS to keep their distance, and Bounding Mana. This is a powerful orb that is sent towards a player, before returning to the Archmage. If you're targeted by this, move if you don't want to take a double-dipping of damage.

If all of that wasn't enough, the Archmage will Mass Polymorph everyone in the room when he's out of mana, taking the opportunity to use Evocation to top himself back up. The polymorph isn't much of an issue in the sense that he won't sling spells at your sheepish selves while channeling Evocation, and if you have the means to get out of it, you can continue your assault.

All we got to see of the gleaming city of Dalaran back in the day was a giant purple dome. This eventually changed with Wrath of the Lich King, but we never got to see its full splendor in Alterac Valley. In World of Warcraft: Forever, the magocratic municipality is fully open to visitors… provided they’re Alliance.

Nonetheless, the City of Daloran dungeon can be cleared by either faction, and it’s a doozy. Starting you off down in the sewers, you’ll make your way up onto its hallowed streets, clearing multiple bosses (and a fair share of trash) in the process. Here, we break down everything you’ll need to successfully navigate CoD, including how to get there, attunement steps, quests, major encounters, and more. We were clearing the instance comfortably at level 30 during the beta, so this stands as our recommended point of entry.

How to get to City of Dalaran

The City of Dalaran is located to the north of Hillsbrad in the Alterac Mountains. The dungeon's entrance is a sewage pipe on the outer side of the northern wall, which leads out onto Lordamere Lake.

There are a couple of routes to the dungeon, and which one you take largely depends on whether you’re Alliance or Horde. If you’re the former, either fly or take a ship into Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills, before heading north-west through the zone, up into Dalaran.

For the latter, the most efficient route is to fly to The Sepulcher and head east to Lordamere Lake. Once you reach The Decrepit Ferry, swim south-east to the dungeon entrance. If you’re over in Kalimdor, simply take the zeppelin from Orgrimmar and run down to the lake from the Undercity. While you can run up from Hillsbrad, which is tempting considering where your attunement chain takes you (more on that in a moment), you'll have to carefully navigate the max-level Kirin Tor guards patrolling the entrance to Dalaran proper.

City of Dalaran Attunement

Before you can enter the dungeon, you’ll first need to get attuned. Well, one person in your group does, at least, as you’re going to need the Dalaran Sewer Key to crack open the pipe and get in.

Unsurprisingly, the Alliance has a much easier time. You’ll first need to go and speak to Emissary Jacques in Southshore, Hillsbrad Foothills (48.3, 60). Likewise, Modera will also cough up the goods for the Horde, though you’ll need to jump through a few more hoops. First, make your way to Tarren Mill, Hillsbrad Foothills, where Magus Wordeen Voidglare (61.6, 20.75) has some work for you. The City of Dalaran is split into two sections. You’ll initially enter through the sewer, making your way through Cantrips & Crows, before crossing over to the other side via The Underbelly. There are a couple of bosses stashed away in the backstreets that are easily missed, so see them away before turning your attention to the grand finale atop The Violet Citadel.

City of Dalaran Quests

Both Alliance and Horde have three faction-exclusive quests apiece. We’ve already mentioned Heart of Disruption, which is offered to players from both. The endpoints and rewards differ, however. Full stat rundowns of reward gear can be found in the loot section of this guide.

Alliance Quests

Most of the Alliance quests are pretty straightforward. For Heart of Disruption, don't forget to loot the Shade of the Archmage at the end of the dungeon to nab the mote. This dropped first time on both toons we ran CoD on, so it should be a guaranteed pickup, though the sample size is too small to tell for sure. As for A Green Sample, Fel Infused Blossoms are found around the central park area -- just make sure you fell the Fel Ancient first. Power Overwhelming, meanwhile, is self-explanatory.

The only quest that's slightly annoying is Starving Arcane. There aren't actually enough of all three mobs in the dungeon to complete it in one run, but the XP and chance at snagging more blues are well worth a second bite at the cherry.

Horde Quests

title: Best WoW: Forever Addons To Download In 2026
summary:
World of Warcraft: Forever and addons go together like Alterac Swiss and the finest bottle of Dalaran Noir. There are a ton of them out there, from major overhauls that completely shake up your UI, to roleplay-bolstering mods that track your journey across Azeroth. Quest helpers, bag managers, and even fishing enhancers, you can switch up almost any aspect of the game.

  • GearQuest Forever
  • Manners
  • Angleur

With thousands of addons out there, many of which having been ported over from Retail and Classic, it’s hard to sort the wheat from the chaff. It’s doubly-difficult to gauge what’s worth using now that Blizzard’s brought its own in-built tools to the fore in the reimagined MMO. Having spent north of 100 hours in Forever’s beta, and a good amount of time hunting for promising new additions to our collection, we’re here to bring you the best WoW: Forever addons to install at launch and beyond.

CurseForge is our go-to WoW addon manager, so the included links will send you that way. That said, you can also download each file as a standalone from there if you prefer to do things manually.

Ellesmere UI

  • Creator: Ellesmere
  • Essential Addon

WoW Forever's UI is as classic as it gets, and the thought of changing that may be sacreligious for some. While Ellesmere UI, ElvUI's spiritual successor, is known for its ultra-sleek, modern layout, the Forever version allows you to maintain a more Vanilla look. Or, if you're after a middle ground, it even boasts a Retail setting.

This is, however, scratching the literal surface of what Ellesmere UI brings to the table. It is absurdly customizable. You can tweak pretty much every interface element to your liking, which is always handy when you're parsing info or reaching for that unbound skill. Considering how much functionality it packs, Ellesmere UI is also surprisingly lightweight, so props to the devs for the optimization work.

BlizzMove

  • Creator: kiatra_

If you're not interested in Ellesmere UI's fanciness, but still desire a little extra manoevurability, BlizzMove has you covered. This handy little addon makes the default frames moveable, so you can drag Forever's myriad windows around as you please.

Cinematic

  • Creator: SapoWoWdev

Azeroth is as visually stunning now as it was 20 years ago, and the UI can often impede your ability to enjoy it. Cinematic gives Forever that Lord of the Rings feel by fading out the UI and bringing in black bars while you're out of combat. You can even keep desired elements hidden while you're blasting down Murlocs, so there's plenty of modularity to be enjoyed.

What's more, Cinematic's camera behaves differently in certain situations. It'll spin around you while hearthing, and sit above your shoulder for a dialogue shot when talking to a quest-giver. There are also a range of filters that'll automatically be applied based on things like weather and time of day.

Immersion

  • Creator: MunkDev

The Vanilla dialogue boxes aren't the prettiest, oftentimes presenting you with a hefty scroll of information that is swiftly disregarded. Immersion fixes that, offering up quest and gossip frames that are infinitely more engaging.

Node Sight

  • Creator: Krelock

Gathering is hardly the most interesting element of WoW Forever, and the default UI does little to help with this. Node Sight not only provides actual images of which herb or ore belongs to each minimap node, but it'll also make it known if it's too-high-a-level for you to snag. For a little extra panache, you can toggle on sparkles for interactable objects in the world, making it easier to spot elements of interest.

SlangSight

  • Creator: pac01722

If you're new to WoW, or have gotten out of touch with the local lingo, SlangSight is here to help you out. Simply mouse over those pesky abbreviations and this addon will immediately tell you what it means. Additionally, you can shift-click a location in chat and it will instantly open the map to where it is. Now you're down with the (middle-aged) kids.

What's Training?

  • Creator: Fusionpit
  • Essential Addon

Without going to a trainer (or opening up a wiki), it's hard to tell what your next levels bring in terms of skill unlocks. We're efficiency fiends here, and What's Training? removes that downtime by adding a simple tab to your spell book that reveals all, including how much it'll cost to learn each ability. Bonus professions functionality has been added in Forever, helping you keep track of available recipes that can be snapped up.

Auctionator

  • Creator: plusmouse
  • Essential Addon

We've been using Auctionator for a long, long time, to the point that we can't actually remember what it's like to use the default Auction House. This addon lets you quickly parse the current market, preventing you from underselling your goods in the process. It'll even show you what your items are worth on the AH with a simple mouse-over, and you can utilize its scan feature to ensure prices are always up-to-date.

Bagnon

  • Creator: jailborc
  • Essential Addon

While Forever's default bag layout isn't bad by any means, Bagnon consolidates those disparate inventories into one, easily-manageable place. If that isn't delightful enough, the addon will further let you keep tabs on what's in your bank and guild vault wherever you are, whatever toon you're playing.

Loot Triage

  • Creator: Krelock

Few things make us let out a deeper sigh than having to declutter our bags so we can loot a shiny new bit of kit, wasting precious seconds as we try and find the cheapest thing to toss. Loot Triage removes the legwork by indicating not only what's junk, but which order you should get rid of it in. It's peak QoL and we absolutely love it.

OpenMap

  • Creator: jigrobbulus
  • Essential Addon

OpenMap is one of our favorite new addons, and for good reason. This beautifully polished map mod presents a seamless, continuous flow as you click, drag, and zoom. This means that, from the world overview, you can scroll all the way into, say Durotar, then into the detailed city map of Orgrimmar. It's essentially Google Maps for WoW Forever, and you can even check out underground paths and dungeon layouts on the fly.

Questie

  • Creator: TheCrux_BB

If you've played WoW for any amount of time, then Questie shouldn't need any introduction. For the unitiated, Questie populates the world map with every available quest within a level range you designate, making it super easy to gauge where to go next in your leveling journey. While it's been considered an essential addon in the past, because Blizzard has added its own feature to Forever that does something similar, we're not so sure now.

That said, you don't quite get the same amount of geographical breadth in the baked-in tool compared to Questie, so it's definitely worth running, even if it's not the must-have it once was.

Forever Quest Pins

  • Creator: murgy

Whereas Questie replaces the default quest tracker, Forever Quest Pins augments it. This addon adds markers to the world map, effectively giving you Questie's functionality with Forever's standard tooling.

Forever Quest Tint

  • Creator: xanastar

WoW Forever adds over 1,000 new quests that didn't exist in Vanilla, and Forever Quest Tint's subtle, teal quest text gradient will let you know if your new fave is a fresh addition. It's a small thing, but it's nice to see where the devs have been cooking.

RareScanner

  • Creator: maqjav
  • Essential Addon

RareScanner has been a go-to addon for as long as we can remember, and it's absolutely going to come in handy throughout your time in Forever. As the name implies, it helps you track rare NPCs, treasures, and events as you play, alerting you when something pops up. Rares can drop some rather nice gear, so it's well worth locking this into your setup. You will need nameplates on for it to work, and you can increase the scanner's range using the command listed in the mod's description.

Follow The Arrow

  • Creator: Harldan

While Forever is designed to be enjoyed at a leisurely pace, you're always going to get the min-maxers seeking out the most efficient leveling route. Follow The Arrow is a true labor of love, with creator 'Harldan' putting in some serious work to provide not only the fastest way to ding, but also detailed instructions on what to do every step of the way.

Road To Sixty

  • Creator: Hotdoghands

Although we commonly shorten 'MMORPG' to 'MMO,' addons like Road to Sixty can really embellish the RP element. As soon as you install it, it will begin tracking your journey across Azerorth, recording your exploits to the world map. The thought of being able to go back and retrace your steps is really quite lovely, so get this one downloaded if you agree.

Social Diary

  • Creator: socialdiary

Similarly to Road to Sixty, Social Diary charts your adventures. However, rather than penning your time on the road to your map, it offers up a comprehensive diary full of memorable moments. In-keeping with its name, this addon places more of an emphasis on your interactions with other players, so you can revel in your journey with your newfound besties while you're gearing up for endgame content.

BiS>Memories

  • Creator: Blankfer

If you'd rather steer clear of extra UI elements while still keeping track of your greatest hits (and misses), BiS>Memories will automatically take a screenshot at key moments. These include each level-up, first boss kills, and even when you finally secure that piece of top-tier loot you'd spent the last couple of weeks grinding for.

Forever Goal Tracker

  • Creator: karlsbad24

It's important to reflect on the past via the above addons, but it's equally-necessary to plan for the future. Forever Goal Tracker lets you set a target, be it gear, an attunement, or a shiny new mount, and provides the necessary steps to reach it. It'll automatically update the planner as you go, making it effortlessly simple to gauge how you're doing.

DungeonJournal

  • Creator: ExehnTV

If you're tired of looking up dungeon loot tables and quest requirements, DungeonJournal has you covered. This neat little addon not only does the aforementioned, but you can also use its in-built dungeon maps to quickly see where each boss is hiding. Used in-tandem with our own Forever dungeon guides, you'll have everything you need to conquer the MMO's new challenges.

Attune

  • Creator: CixiDelmont
  • Essential Addon

Attune is a cracking little addon that makes coordinating attunements with your guildies nice and easy. It'll show you all the steps you need to take to get dungeon or raid-ready, and share your progress with your comrades. It's not so important if you're running content solo, but it's highly-recommended if you're grouping up with the gang.

ItemTree

  • Creator: rockjawbonesnapperco

WoW Forever has a lot of items, and it's sometimes hard to tell from a glance how beneficial they are. ItemTree ties everything together with a neat little bow, making it incredibly easy to see not only how your existing items tie into professions, quests, etc., but also where to find components you're looking for. If you're running Enchanting, it'll also tell you exactly what materials you'll get for disenchanting stuff -- nice.

Reverse Engineering

  • Creator: IAmChlls

If you're in the midst of profession leveling, then Reverse Engineering is a godsend. This addon calculates all the materials you need for item crafting, adjusting dynamically as you gather the goods. It even accounts for parent items, saving you unnecessary headaches. We're writers, not mathematicians, so this gets a big thumbs-up from us.

GearQuest Forever

  • Creator: weber8210

If you wish to achieve maximum power at every step of your Forever leveling journey, GearQuest Forever ensures you're always at your best. Once installed, you'll be able to find upgrades for every gear slot and where to find them. The addon's recommendations can be tweaked based on your playstyle. Don't like dungeons? GearQuest Forever will forget about them at the click of a button.

Manners

  • Creator: fpsacha

Trading buffs with random players is one of those micro-social interactions that make WoW so great. Sometimes, however, a mage will drop you an Arcane Intellect, blinking off into the sunset before you're able to return the favor -- feels bad, man. Manners logs these interactions, and pops a one-tap button on your UI that will instantly buff a player back. It's a small thing, but it's good for the soul.

Angleur

  • Creator: Legolando

Of course, we've saved the best addon for last -- we definitely aren't fishing minigame fiends. If this wonderfully scuffed trailer isn't enough to instantly convince you to install Angleur, let's talk specifics. This addon basically lets you do all things fishing with a single button, including triggering macros. Auras and custom timers help you keep track of buffs, and you can even adjust the audio to better hear when the big kahuna's snapped up your bait.

  • DungeonJournal
  • Attune
  • ItemTree
  • Reverse Engineering
  • GearQuest Forever
  • Manners
  • Angleur

With thousands of addons out there, many of which having been ported over from Retail and Classic, it’s hard to sort the wheat from the chaff. It’s doubly-difficult to gauge what’s worth using now that Blizzard’s brought its own in-built tools to the fore in the reimagined MMO. Having spent north of 100 hours in Forever’s beta, and a good amount of time hunting for promising new additions to our collection, we’re here to bring you the best WoW: Forever addons to install at launch and beyond.

CurseForge is our go-to WoW addon manager, so the included links will send you that way. That said, you can also download each file as a standalone from there if you prefer to do things manually.

Ellesmere UI

  • Creator: Ellesmere
  • Essential Addon

WoW Forever's UI is as classic as it gets, and the thought of changing that may be sacreligious for some. While Ellesmere UI, ElvUI's spiritual successor, is known for its ultra-sleek, modern layout, the Forever version allows you to maintain a more Vanilla look. Or, if you're after a middle ground, it even boasts a Retail setting.

This is, however, scratching the literal surface of what Ellesmere UI brings to the table. It is absurdly customizable. You can tweak pretty much every interface element to your liking, which is always handy when you're parsing info or reaching for that unbound skill. Considering how much functionality it packs, Ellesmere UI is also surprisingly lightweight, so props to the devs for the optimization work.

BlizzMove

  • Creator: kiatra_

If you're not interested in Ellesmere UI's fanciness, but still desire a little extra manoevurability, BlizzMove has you covered. This handy little addon makes the default frames moveable, so you can drag Forever's myriad windows around as you please.

Cinematic

  • Creator: SapoWoWdev

Azeroth is as visually stunning now as it was 20 years ago, and the UI can often impede your ability to enjoy it. Cinematic gives Forever that Lord of the Rings feel by fading out the UI and bringing in black bars while you're out of combat. You can even keep desired elements hidden while you're blasting down Murlocs, so there's plenty of modularity to be enjoyed.

Immersion

  • Creator: MunkDev

The Vanilla dialogue boxes aren't the prettiest, oftentimes presenting you with a hefty scroll of information that is swiftly disregarded. Immersion fixes that, offering up quest and gossip frames that are infinitely more engaging.

  • Creator: Krelock

Gathering is hardly the most interesting element of WoW Forever, and the default UI does little to help with this. Node Sight not only provides actual images of which herb or ore belongs to each minimap node, but it'll also make it known if it's too-high-a-level for you to snag. SlangSight

  • Creator: pac01722

If you're new to WoW, or have gotten out of touch with the local lingo, SlangSight is here to help you out. Simply mouse over those pesky abbreviations and this addon will immediately tell you what it means. Additionally, you can shift-click a location in chat and it will instantly open the map to where it is. Now you're down with the (middle-aged) kids.

  • Creator: Fusionpit
  • Essential Addon

Without going to a trainer (or opening up a wiki), it's hard to tell what your next levels bring in terms of skill unlocks. Auctionator

  • Creator: plusmouse
  • Essential Addon

We've been using Auctionator for a long, long time, to the point that we can't actually remember what it's like to use the default Auction House. Bagnon

  • Creator: jailborc
  • Essential Addon

While Forever's default bag layout isn't bad by any means, Bagnon consolidates those disparate inventories into one, easily-manageable place.   • Essential Addon

While it's been considered an essential addon in the past, because Blizzard has added its own feature to Forever that does something similar, we're not so sure now.

That said, you don't quite get the same amount of geographical breadth in the baked-in tool compared to Questie, so it's definitely worth running, even if it's not the must-have it once was.

  • Creator: murgy

Whereas Questie replaces the default quest tracker, Forever Quest Pins augments it. This addon adds markers to the world map, effectively giving you Questie's functionality with Forever's standard tooling.

  • Creator: xanastar

WoW Forever adds over 1,000 new quests that didn't exist in Vanilla, and Forever Quest Tint's subtle, teal quest text gradient will let you know if your new fave is a fresh addition. It's a small thing, but it's nice to see where the devs have been cooking.

  • Creator: maqjav
  • Essential Addon

RareScanner has been a go-to addon for as long as we can remember, and it's absolutely going to come in handy throughout your time in Forever. Rares can drop some rather nice gear, so it's well worth locking this into your setup. Follow The Arrow

  • Creator: Harldan

While Forever is designed to be enjoyed at a leisurely pace, you're always going to get the min-maxers seeking out the most efficient leveling route. Follow The Arrow is a true labor of love, with creator 'Harldan' putting in some serious work to provide not only the fastest way to ding, but also detailed instructions on what to do every step of the way.

Road To Sixty

  • Creator: Hotdoghands

Although we commonly shorten 'MMORPG' to 'MMO,' addons like Road to Sixty can really embellish the RP element. As soon as you install it, it will begin tracking your journey across Azerorth, recording your exploits to the world map. The thought of being able to go back and retrace your steps is really quite lovely, so get this one downloaded if you agree.

Social Diary

  • Creator: socialdiary

Similarly to Road to Sixty, Social Diary charts your adventures. However, rather than penning your time on the road to your map, it offers up a comprehensive diary full of memorable moments. In-keeping with its name, this addon places more of an emphasis on your interactions with other players, so you can revel in your journey with your newfound besties while you're gearing up for endgame content.

BiS>Memories

  • Creator: Blankfer

If you'd rather steer clear of extra UI elements while still keeping track of your greatest hits (and misses), BiS>Memories will automatically take a screenshot at key moments. These include each level-up, first boss kills, and even when you finally secure that piece of top-tier loot you'd spent the last couple of weeks grinding for.

Forever Goal Tracker

  • Creator: karlsbad24

It's important to reflect on the past via the above addons, but it's equally-necessary to plan for the future. Forever Goal Tracker lets you set a target, be it gear, an attunement, or a shiny new mount, and provides the necessary steps to reach it. It'll automatically update the planner as you go, making it effortlessly simple to gauge how you're doing.

DungeonJournal

  • Creator: ExehnTV

If you're tired of looking up dungeon loot tables and quest requirements, DungeonJournal has you covered. This neat little addon not only does the aforementioned, but you can also use its in-built dungeon maps to quickly see where each boss is hiding. Used in-tandem with our own Forever dungeon guides, you'll have everything you need to conquer the MMO's new challenges.

Attune

  • Creator: CixiDelmont
  • Essential Addon

Attune is a cracking little addon that makes coordinating attunements with your guildies nice and easy. It'll show you all the steps you need to take to get dungeon or raid-ready, and share your progress with your comrades. It's not so important if you're running content solo, but it's highly-recommended if you're grouping up with the gang.

ItemTree

  • Creator: rockjawbonesnapperco

WoW Forever has a lot of items, and it's sometimes hard to tell from a glance how beneficial they are. ItemTree ties everything together with a neat little bow, making it incredibly easy to see not only how your existing items tie into professions, quests, etc., but also where to find components you're looking for. If you're running Enchanting, it'll also tell you exactly what materials you'll get for disenchanting stuff -- nice.

Reverse Engineering

  • Creator: IAmChlls

If you're in the midst of profession leveling, then Reverse Engineering is a godsend. This addon calculates all the materials you need for item crafting, adjusting dynamically as you gather the goods. It even accounts for parent items, saving you unnecessary headaches. We're writers, not mathematicians, so this gets a big thumbs-up from us.

GearQuest Forever

  • Creator: weber8210

If you wish to achieve maximum power at every step of your Forever leveling journey, GearQuest Forever ensures you're always at your best. Once installed, you'll be able to find upgrades for every gear slot and where to find them. The addon's recommendations can be tweaked based on your playstyle. Don't like dungeons? GearQuest Forever will forget about them at the click of a button.

Manners

  • Creator: fpsacha

Trading buffs with random players is one of those micro-social interactions that make WoW so great. Sometimes, however, a mage will drop you an Arcane Intellect, blinking off into the sunset before you're able to return the favor -- feels bad, man. Manners logs these interactions, and pops a one-tap button on your UI that will instantly buff a player back. It's a small thing, but it's good for the soul.

Angleur

  • Creator: Legolando

Of course, we've saved the best addon for last -- we definitely aren't fishing minigame fiends. If this wonderfully scuffed trailer isn't enough to instantly convince you to install Angleur, let's talk specifics. This addon basically lets you do all things fishing with a single button, including triggering macros. Auras and custom timers help you keep track of buffs, and you can even adjust the audio to better hear when the big kahuna's snapped up your bait.

title: Super Smash Bros. Was The Best Thing To Ever Happen To Fire Emblem
summary:
Booting up Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave had me feeling nostalgic. Fire Emblem as it is now would’ve been surreal to six-year-old me, who only knew “Marth and Roy from Smash.” Back then, Fire Emblem was still a niche series in the west and many of us had no idea who they were. Little did I know, these swordsmen would just be two of many Fire Emblem heroes to join the fighting game series, and Fire Emblem games would reach mainstream popularity.

I discovered Fire Emblem in the early 2000s when I first started playing Super Smash Bros. Melee on our clunky big-screen TV in the basement. It was my favorite game to play with my cousins outside of having them watch me play single-player games like Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly and The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker. We played Melee for hours that summer of 2001, eventually unlocking Marth, the blue-haired prince from the 1990's Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light. After that, we unlocked Roy, the protagonist of 2002's Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade. 

Marth and Roy do have voicelines, but they are all in Japanese. I mostly remember just the grunting sounds they would make from swinging around their swords, anyway. Maybe it’s because of that that the Smash fandom invented personalities for both fighters in fanfics and comics until their games were released in the west and set things straight. Link also showed up in many of these creations, maybe because he’s the only other Super Smash swordsman from that era. 

Most of the fan-made stories that I remember from that time came from Fanfiction.net and Deviantart. CallistoHime, the author of fanfics like Time Cannot Erase, admits that she filled in the blanks because she had little to go off of besides Marth’s Smash Bros. profile. One artist I followed back then, Katie Tiedrich, also made a comic about the gap between her interpretation of Marth and the real thing. These are just a few examples from what was a relatively small community in the mid-to-late 2000s.

Nintendo Magazine cites Marth and Roy’s inclusion in Smash Bros. as a driving reason to release the Fire Emblem games in the west, starting with Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade, where Roy was the protagonist. In an Iwata Asks interview, Fire Emblem producer Tohru Narihiro even thanked Masahiro Sakurai for his work on Smash Bros. because of the fighting game franchise's impact on the international popularity of the previously niche RPG series.

“Thanks to your work, the reputations of Marth and Ike have grown beyond our expectations,” he said (2008's Super Smash Bros. Brawl had already come out when he made this comment, and 2005's Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance protagonist Ike was included in the roster instead of Roy).

Since the addition of Marth and Roy in Melee, adding new Fire Emblem characters to Smash has become somewhat of a tradition for the fighting game series. As mentioned earlier, Ike joined the roster in Brawl. Then, 2014's Smash 4 not only saw Roy return to the roster, but it also added Fire Emblem Awakening's Lucina and Robin. 2018's Ultimate really reflects how popular Fire Emblem was becoming, including all aforementioned characters and then also adding Awakening's Chrom, Fates' Corrin, and Three Houses' Byleth. 

As Fire Emblem's presence in the Smash roster has grown, so has the popularity (and quality!) of the games. The first Fire Emblem to be localized for international audiences, The Blazing Blade, released in 2003. Several years (and Fire Emblem releases) later, Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon would come out in 2009, and the fanbase outside Japan finally got to see Marth’s backstory. Rather than the moody prince we imagined, Marth is a kindhearted leader who is looking for allies to assist him in taking back his kingdom from an evil dragon. 

At the time, I was less enthusiastic about learning about Marth and more locked into Shadow Dragon's gameplay of training units and strategically placing them on the map during battle. Marth was the catalyst for me to pick up my first Fire Emblem game, but the gameplay itself is what I fell in love with. It still wasn’t good enough to rocket the series into critical acclaim, but thanks to the growing popularity of Fire Emblem, we steadily got more and more games in the series. 

Looking back, Shadow Dragon isn’t even what I would consider “one of the good ones” when it comes to Fire Emblem. The five Fire Emblem games that came out between Melee and Shadow Dragon--The Binding Blade, The Blazing Blade, The Sacred Stones, Path of Radiance, and Radiant Dawn--didn’t garner much attention from the mainstream. The shift from niche to noteworthy happened when Fire Emblem: Awakening introduced a fully fleshed out support system and life-sim gameplay that hooked me on its characters. 

Then, Fire Emblem: Three Houses further improved this formula with a branching narrative that actually felt cohesive and morally complicated--so much so that players still fight about which of the titular three houses was “right” years later. Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave refines this formula even farther, with a way to easily swap between the stories of its four protagonists. 

This isn't to say that all of the games have been hits since Awakening. I wanted to love Fates, which also featured a branching narrative with DLC branches that you needed to buy, but the conflict was black and white without much room for moral interpretation and Corrin was pacifistic to a fault. FE3H was essentially everything I wanted from Fates but didn’t get.

However, at this point, Fire Emblem sells itself. In recent years, Fire Emblem: Three Houses was given the Player’s Voice Award at The Game Awards 2020. Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave is equally if not more ambitious, earning a 9/10 in GameSpot's review and an 89 on Metacritic. It’s now common to find players who have discovered the series through the sheer push of its own popularity rather than piggybacking off the advertising of a popular fighting game. 

It’s been over 25 years since Marth and Roy debuted in Melee and, even now, watching how much Fire Emblem blew up over it is an overwhelming feeling.

title: Former Xbox Exec Shares Her Side Of The Story After Mysterious Depature
summary:
Helen Chiang, the veteran Xbox staffer who got promoted in July and left the company amid mysterious circumstances just recently, has shared her side of the story--but her response doesn't close the book on this saga.

In a LinkedIn post titled "Clarity is Kindess," which itself is a reference to her former boss (and Xbox CEO) Asha Sharma's much-ridiculed and cringey mantra, said it's "not accurate" that she was "fired for a policy violation" as multiple reports said.

Chiang said she will not "turn this into a play-by-play" and reveal the specifics, but she wanted to speak out to dispel rumors. "What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize."

She went on to "set the record straight" by claiming she did not leak confidential company information to the press as some had speculated. "I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I’ve done as part of my job," she said, adding that this includes having no contact with any journalist who reached out to her before today to ask for her side of the story.

Chiang went on to say she did not leave Xbox to join a competitor. "You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build," she said

"Xbox was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here," she said.  

That may all be true, but it's also unquestionable that people regularly spend lengthy periods of their career at one company, in high-level positions, and then move to other companies.

Third, Chiang said she "did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity."

"I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record," she said.

Chiang added that she did not leave Xbox because she was "passed over for a bigger role." She said that since having children, she became more "intentional about how I define ambition and success." She said she has purposefully not sought out bigger roles or jobs with more responsibilities; she said she hadn't interviewed for a job since 2011.

"My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact," she said, adding that she did not ask to become Xbox's first-ever COO.

"I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently," she said.

Chiang said she has "serious concerns" about how those standards were applied in her case, and she said those concerns "deserve to be taken seriously."

"I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard," she said. "That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind."

Chiang's statement doesn't spell out the specific nature surrounding her departure from Xbox, so many will naturally want more answers. Those could come in time, as Chiang said this is "not the whole story."

Another former Xbox executive, Shannon Loftis, commented on Chiang's post to say she is "Team Helen all the way." Loftis said she wonders who may have leaked the "false information" about Chiang and what their motivations may have been. In any event, she says it shows a "loss of moral character and 'clarity' in leadership at Xbox."

"A real leadership team would have relentlessly pursued the 'leaker' and taken appropriate action because 'confidential personnel matters' actually are bases for defamation lawsuits," she said. "It's a clownshow up in there and I feel terrible for anyone that still has to deal with it."

A spokesperson for Microsoft told Windows Central that the company does not “discuss individual personnel matters.”

According to a source speaking to Eurogamer, Chiang was “terminated for policy violations.” The Verge’s Tom Warren backed this up, saying Chiang was cut loose due to a “policy violation,” but the exact nature of that is unknown.

In July, Sharma announced that Chiang would become Xbox’s first-ever COO, with “end-to-end” responsibility for the financial future of Xbox’s content, hardware, platform, and services.

Chiang had worked at Microsoft for 20 years, in that time playing a key role in the creation of Xbox Live and later shepherding Mojang and the lucrative Minecraft franchise. As COO, Chiang was expected to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results,” Sharma said.

For her part, Sharma said she will have an update to share on the COO position at Xbox at some point, but she didn’t divulge more.

The Xbox business was “not healthy” when Sharma took over, she said, and Chiang no doubt had a challenging road ahead of her. As for now, however, people can only speculate as to the real reason she left Xbox.
